Alicia M: Quick design review — thinking of moving the token counter out of the bottom-right corner and into the composer toolbar so users see usage while streaming. Screenshot: https://redwood.design/proto/stream-token-placement :thought_balloon: Samir K: I like the discoverability idea, but worried about visual clutter when responses stream rapidly. What if it collapses to a tiny pill that expands on hover/focus? :thinking_face: Marta P: Accessibility nits: screen readers shouldn't get token counts every few seconds. We should only announce meaningful state changes (stream started, interrupted, finished) and explicit actions (regenerate). Suggest an aria-live region with polite setting and debounced updates. Example: ```html
Streaming…
``` Also we need a visible focus ring for the token pill when keyboard navigated and an obvious label for the interrupt action (Stop vs Interrupt vs Pause). Zoe L: UX question — semantics of stop vs pause. From support logs, users expect "Stop" to abort and let them edit the prompt, not resume mid-stream. "Pause" implies resumable buffer which we don't support. Recommend labeling: "Stop (Interrupt)" during proto and use tooltip for details. Samir K: Agree on wording. For keyboard shortcuts, propose: Esc = interrupt currently streaming generation, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter = regenerate. Make sure these are documented in the composer help. Alicia M: For the token counter itself: two modes. Compact shows just a token icon + number (e.g., 512), expanded shows tokens used / max and estimated remaining. Tooltip on hover reveals breakdown (prompt vs response estimate). In streaming collapse to just icon to avoid jitter. Marta P: Implementation detail: avoid changing layout during stream to prevent content jump — keep counter width fixed and animate internal numbers. Use CSS like: ```css .token-pill { width: 64px; display: inline-flex; justify-content: center; } .token-count { transition: transform 150ms ease; } ``` And for SR announce only on important transitions: - "Generation started" - "Generation interrupted by user" - "Generation complete — X tokens used" This keeps verbosity down for assistive tech. Zoe L: Visual contrast: the current green pill fails 3:1 for the small token text. Need 4.5:1. I'll drop a palette suggestion in Figma. :paintbrush: designbot: Preview deploy up at https://playground-preview.red/streams/1755001234 — includes compact pill + keyboard shortcuts. Use #design-test for feedback. Samir K: Tiny interaction nit — when user presses Stop, we should show a subtle snackbar: "Generation stopped — partial result available. Press R to regenerate." This reduces confusion. :bell: Alicia M: Good call. Also adding a tiny affordance in the prompt library: quick-insert for last-used system prompt next to the token pill so power users can swap context quickly while monitoring tokens. Marta P: One more a11y check: if quick-insert opens a small dialog, ensure focus trap and that Escape closes it and returns focus to composer. Zoe L: I'll mock variations: pill-left vs pill-right vs inline-center and test with 6 people for preference tomorrow. If no one objects, we'll land compact pill on the right of the composer toolbar and keep keyboard focus order: composer input -> token pill -> send button. Alicia M: Sounds good. Next step: Zoe to post Figma with contrast options + micro-interactions, Marta to add aria spec, Samir to wire up shortcuts in the prototype, I'll follow up on copy for tooltips. :thumbsup:
